p: Nelson Street sits in the middle of Grainger Town, the elegant run of 19th-century streets that gives Newcastle centre its handsome look. Step outside and you're minutes from Grey's Monument, the sweeping curve of Grey Street and the Theatre Royal, so it's easy to slot a session in before or after a show.

Hungry before the darts? The Grainger Market is right on the doorstep and has been feeding the city for well over 150 years, with stalls selling everything from cheap snacks to fresh produce. The Laing Art Gallery is a short walk away if you fancy a bit of culture first, and St James' Park, home of Newcastle United, looms over the top of town, which makes this a handy meeting point on a match day.

Getting there is straightforward. Monument Metro station is a couple of minutes' walk, and Newcastle Central Station is close enough to stroll to, so it works well for groups arriving from Sunderland, the coast or further afield.
Allow a couple of hours if you're making a meal of it, and arrive a bit before your slot so the whole group is there when the first game starts.
